The snow-covered landscape and bitter cold made following the trail of the Creature a difficult and time-consuming endeavor.
It took months of preparation, but even as I set out upon this blasted hunt to seek revenge against the abomination, I was not quite sure which way to venture.
A hard journey lay ahead. While my body was weary from the excursion, the hatred in my heart fueled me as I awoke each morning searching for any sign of the Creature's activities.
They claim to have seen their foul sneers from the darkness, orchestrating this entire farce!
They state that they hope now that their hideous secrets will come to light!

This fortified district offers little in the way of investment, so I'm afraid to admit that I have begun a partnership with the local shipping company. What it lacks in potential, I believe it makes up for in expediency. I swear to you my visits there are brief and lawful, for I am as always a dutiful citizen.

What is this place? It is certainly not much from the exterior, but considering the locale, I have very little choice in the matter. It provides me access to goods otherwise inaccessible, and while the stench is sometimes severe - both of the building and its inhabitants - this is all I require.

I ask you to disregard the rumors that I have merely invested capital into this venture to gain illicit produce. It is a humble shipping dock and my visits during the evening are simply to assess matters of inventory. I take offense to any suggestions otherwise.
Creating life against my will only to feed the urges of a hideous fiend? Am I forced to forever suffer for the sins of my family? What good can come from aiding the devil's work?
I curse my grandfather for thrusting this abomination into the world and dooming us to accommodate its unnatural wants. Oh, how the sorrow encompasses me!
I am nothing if not thorough.
I sometimes cannot contain my genius.

With distinct gothic style, a robust gate and fencing stretching the perimeter of the plot and an entryway leading towards a dual staircase carpetted with crimson linens of the finest quality, the decor struck me as appropriately imposing.

I was particularly struck by the fine, gray exterior with hip and gable roofing structures and metal spires. A proper gentleman of distinguished inclinations - and wealth to match - no doubt resided within.
I could distinctly see fine hairs growing from the center of his palm as he talked.
He leaned forward, speaking with a coarse whisper and I could smell a rankness in his breath.

The cerebellum is especially sensitive to a concentrated electrical shock. While the singed skin and hair produce a noxious smell, the effectiveness is undeniable.
I'm afraid I must be obstinate in the nature of my offer.
I'm terribly beside myself that we could not come to firm agreement.

Well, it appears you have me at a disadvantage since I extended the invitation. How about I put in a good word with my charge at the Town Hall? I'm sure it would be nice to have some of your scientific achievements recognized by the public.

I was wise to contact you. You are unlike the other buffoons who would simply agree to any offer thrown at them. If I cannot tempt you with a monetary deal, perhaps my clout in academia will sway you. I will be sure to advertise your name to the universities in London upon my next visit.

My unending spirit of invention, it once again leads the ignorant to my doorstep.

I have planned for a grave plot to be installed upon the estate grounds to keep my remains from being contaminated in death by those who never accepted me in life. Yes, I take full responsibility for the rift this will cause between myself and the whole superstitious lot. Damn those insufferable peons!

I refuse to mend bridges built between myself and these simpletons. Why would I risk the inevitable defilement of our esteemed heritage in a public cemetery? My family will be buried upon my own lands by my own terms! I deserve to rest in peace while they deserve to rot in a hell of their own creation!

Inspection day: Wore newest overcoat, but received no compliment from the reprobates attending the door. At least the security was lax enough that I was given no physical inspection upon entering the ramshackle government office.

Dismal afternoon - overcast with a dreadful scud blanketing the town in grayness. When I arrived at the Town Hall for the scheduled inspection, I could only shake my head at the single individual in a recently re-stitched military uniform left-over from the 18th Century, sleeping at his post by the wooden double-doors. I decided to enter without rousing him to avoid investing any more time in my visit.

Shoddy. Regrettable. The Town Hall was all cobwebs and cracked plaster, with a set of ancient benches with black mold along the bases. The musty offices where I was to confirm my existence were in no better condition.

I received no cordial greeting. I received no additional bonus for my willingness to betray my own morals and submit to this oppressive occupation. I barely received the pleasantries of a greeting aside from a disinterested grunt from a sack-suited barrister loitering in the periphery. A clerk bid me sit with a handwave and it was an hour before the person handling my paperwork appeared.

Like a mangy hound, I was summarily dismissed and sent away after a brief glance at my papers and a lengthy interrogation. The officer in question was obviously less intent on law enforcement and more prone to surveying one's character with his eyes.

The interrogation was lengthy and lasted into the early evening. The individual in charge of my case had apparently been relishing the opportunity to 'nail me to the wall' as it were, and when my answers proved adequate and level-headed, the line of questioning became more aggressive. Did he think me a fool?

args.lit: The grounds of the old jail appeared even more imposing than they had been when the inmates were enclosed inside its iron walls. I made sure that my visit was brief, but with delinquent eyes upon me and obscene messages written on the walls in crude scarlet streaks, it was certainly not made short enough.

As I arrived at the steps of the Junk Palace, I was greeted by a rough guard wearing an apron fashioned with protective scraps of steel. 'Nice to meat you,' the man who introduced himself as 'Grinder' said. 'I have no beef with you.' And so I gained entrance to this decaying institution where the walls fall to pieces and metal springs from the Earth.

The Count and what appeared to be several visitors sharing similar, friendly, yet distant demeanors urged me towards a sumptuous banquet table arranged as if my presence had been expected that very evening. I dined upon portions of creamed pheasant, black puddings, ostropel, and a healthy share of plum brandy. The food was so varied and rich that I was surprised that when the courses waned a hunger still remained with me.

The Count's attendant ushered me into the study, where the gentleman relaxed in a daychair sipping from a glass full of deep red wine. He bid me sit and we talked for many minutes as I observed the mahogany shelves that lined the room, overloaded with books that appeared so new the spines had not been cracked.

There was no one there to greet me on that day. As seemed fitting, for this was not some achievement to be unlocked - it was a personal decision that had long tore at the fiber of my being.
Though the appointed time had come, I did not attend the event. In fact, I spent most of my day lost in thought. It was something I should have done a long time ago.
I will allow my thoughts to spread like tendrils of ivy, gleaning every ounce of sunlight from the gloom that surrounds me.
I will allow the seed of genius to germinate in whatever fertile soil I deem necessary.
Only the whistle of the wind and the scent of azaleas.
Only a cold, gray stillness and low-hanging clouds against an oppressive sky.
